intro.title: Welcome to Azrou — cedars and macaques
intro.p1: Azrou sits in Morocco's Middle Atlas, a mountain town named after the Amazigh word for rock. It is the practical base for cedar forests, Barbary macaque sightings and cool air between Fez, Meknes and the road toward Midelt or Beni Mellal.
intro.p2: The town itself is low-key: a weekly souk, a central rock landmark and easy access to forest tracks. Plan one or two nights if you want a forest morning, macaques and a quieter contrast to the imperial cities.

cedars.title: Cedar forest
cedars.p1: The cedar forests around Azrou are the main reason travellers stop. Tall Atlas cedars, cool shade and forest tracks sit a short drive from the centre — one of the most accessible mountain landscapes in the Middle Atlas.
cedars.p2: Go early for softer light and fewer cars. Stay on marked or commonly used tracks and leave no litter; the forest is shared with wildlife and local users.
cedars.tip: Combine with macaque spotting the same morning. Dress in layers — shade is cool even in summer.

macaques.title: Barbary macaques
macaques.p1: Barbary macaques live in the forests near Azrou. Sightings are common on popular forest roads, but they are wild animals — not a zoo.
macaques.p2: Do not feed them. Keep food packed away, give them space and avoid close selfies. Feeding changes behaviour and can be risky for both people and monkeys.
macaques.tip: Morning visits are often quieter. A guide is optional but can help with respectful viewing.

rock.title: Azrou rock & centre
rock.p1: Azrou takes its name from a large rock in the centre — a simple landmark that orients the compact mountain town.
rock.p2: Use the centre for cafés, supplies and a short walk before or after the forest. It is functional rather than a long sightseeing circuit.
rock.tip: Good base for a coffee after a forest morning.

souk.title: Souk & local life
souk.p1: Azrou's souk brings mountain-town energy on market days — produce, livestock and local trade rather than a polished tourist bazaar.
souk.p2: Confirm the market day when you arrive. Go early, dress modestly and ask before close-up photos of people.
souk.tip: Pair with a centre walk the same day.

forest_walks.title: Forest walks & viewpoints
forest_walks.p1: Short walks and roadside clearings around the cedar zone give Atlas air, views and a slower pace than the imperial cities.
forest_walks.p2: Wear sturdy shoes, carry water and check weather — mountain conditions change quickly, especially outside summer.
forest_walks.tip: Late afternoon light is soft on the cedars.

ifrane_link.title: Road to Ifrane
ifrane_link.p1: Ifrane sits a short drive from Azrou — a planned mountain town with a different feel, often used as a combined Middle Atlas stop.
ifrane_link.p2: Easy as a half-day or an overnight if you want both forest (Azrou) and the cooler, structured streets of Ifrane.
ifrane_link.tip: Self-drive or grand taxi; allow time for forest stops on the way.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Azrou?
q1.answer: One night covers a forest morning and the centre; two nights if you want Ifrane and a slower mountain pace.

q2.question: Where can I see Barbary macaques?
q2.answer: In the cedar forests near Azrou, often along popular forest roads. Observe from a distance and never feed them.

q3.question: How do I get to Azrou?
q3.answer: By road from Fez or Meknes (about 1.5–2 hours). Grands taxis and buses serve the route; a car is flexible for forest stops.

q4.question: Is Azrou cold?
q4.answer: Cooler than the plains year-round. Bring layers; winter can be cold with possible snow on higher ground.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for cedar forests, macaques and Middle Atlas air without rushing.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Drive or taxi to the cedar stands near Azrou while the light is soft. Walk shaded tracks and listen for the forest before the weekend traffic builds.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Watch for macaques along popular forest roads. Keep food packed away, give them space and never feed them — they are wild animals, not a zoo attraction.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Return to the centre by the rock landmark. Café, simple grill and an early night after the mountain air.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Short hop to Ifrane for a different Middle Atlas face: planned streets, cooler air and a slower town walk.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Stay in Ifrane for parks and cafés, or loop back toward quieter forest clearings if you prefer nature over town.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Hearty tagine or grill back in Azrou — cooler evenings call for warmer plates.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Another forest track if the weather is clear, or the weekly souk if it falls on your day — mountain-town energy rather than a tourist bazaar.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Depart toward Fez for the imperial medina, or south toward Midelt and the High Atlas approach if your route continues that way.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: A final café stop in Azrou or on the road — simple close to a short Middle Atlas chapter.
